newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer, may target resistance.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer, may target resistance.

text.p: Precious metal prices added to Tuesday's slightly firmer levels on Wednesday morning, raising the possibility of a challenge to overhead resistance by the end of the week, dealers said.
But business was likely to be fairly routine ahead of the over the counter (OTC) option expiry on Thursday afternoon.
Gold fixed at $383.25 per ounce against $382.30 on Tuesday and a close then of $381.80/$382.30.
About 70 cents was added later in New York, most of which was retained in the Tokyo and Hong Kong markets, where business was light and currency related, dealers said.
Bullion showed little response to the U.S. Federal Reserve Bank leaving the fed funds and discount rates unchanged at 5.25 and five per cent respectively.
The Federal Open Market Committee which met yesterday had been widely touted to favour a 25-basis point rise.
"Gold has recovered reasonably well as yesterday's short covering continues. Potentially there is a bigger rally in gold than there is in silver," a dealer said.
He added that more new short positions had been built in gold than silver (on Comex) as witnessed by a declining RSI and rising open interest.
Even so, other dealers warned that there were sell orders lurking above the market and some unhedged houses were potential sellers if the price moved substantially over $383.00.
"Most people are just trying to play in currencies by making deals against the cross," one dealer said.
Dealers largely dismissed the OTC option expiry on Thursday as having a market influence given that gold was in the middle of the main strike prices at $380.00 and $385.00.
"It's been a long time since an option expiry influenced prices," one dealer commented.
Dealers said silver was likely to be limited to a $4.90-$4.96 range today and follow gold, but it had less rallying potential than the yellow metal.
"Silver is short but it is not as short as gold," one dealer said, while others noted the possibility of short selling to come in silver.
It was quoted at $4.94/$4.96, up six cents from the close.

Platinum also rallied slightly to be indicated at $388.25/$389.25, up $2.15, but dealing was quiet with some spread trading seen against gold. Palladium was $1.75 up at $118.75/$119.75. -Brian Spoors, London newsroom +44 171 542 8058
